text: asked QC5-001: J's ruling 4 (15 October) asks that the C5b packets carry the rule and the amended declarations with their members' quotes. Each packet must also hold account.md, figure-C5.md and propositions.jsonl (35,073 bytes), the instruction and three rooms under the 51,200-byte ceiling. The 36 amended declarations, whole, come to about 40 KB before their quotes, so they do not fit even split across the three readers. I served instead: the rule (its reading parts and the C5a-02 scope paragraph); the 40 sentences of all 36 declarations that hold a word from the rule's lists, which are the sentences the rule puts in question, split by declaration across the readers, each reader saying whether each sentence stands; and the 72 Stigmergy records drawn at C5a-01, 24 per reader, to code blind. Ten declarations have no sentence in question and are not served (Keying, Sensemaking, Collective efficacy, Reciprocity, Neo-tribes, Completion ritual, Collective memory, Transition, Critical mass, Contention). Not served: the whole declarations, their other sentences and the quotes those carry. To fit, the three rooms are served as their facts and 7 passages each by cite.py's seeded draw, without their forests. Is this an acceptable second reading for J's ruling 4? If not, which should give way: the rooms' passages, or a further reader for the whole declarations after the dispatch? | meanwhile: The packets go out as built, and the dispatch can run on them. The check leg scores the readers' sentence verdicts and codes against mine. If you rule otherwise, the packets are rebuilt before the dispatch, or the remaining declarations go to the reader you name.

The three packets built (packets.py files --stage C5): C5-reader-1 50,993 bytes, C5-reader-2 51,018, C5-reader-3 51,035, under the 51,200 ceiling. Each holds 0-read-me-first.md (served sha256 of account.md 77b5e35d..., the instruction verbatim, the second reading), account.md, figure-C5.md, propositions.jsonl, rooms.md (cardinals, luciomains, mysterydungeon: facts and 7 seeded passages each) and second-reading.md (the rule; that reader's share of the 40 sentences in question; the Stigmergy code definitions and the 24 records of one member theme, blind). Each carries the end line; none names my notes. run_manifest.json's C5 entry pins the packets' sha256. QC5-001 asks the handler whether the sentences in question are an acceptable second reading of the declarations for J's ruling 4; meanwhile the packets go out as built.

figure-C5.md: the paragraph on what it leaves out named the tentative arrow A21 by id, and the check reads every arrow id in the figure as drawn (two errors: no instance, not in the model). It now names the arrow by its ends (P08 to P21). The figure was written again, the three packets rebuilt (50,998, 51,023 and 51,040 bytes), and the C5 manifest entry's digests read again (c5b_manifest_entry.py --packets). validate.py C5: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Close of C5b, the readers' build. run_manifest.json C5 entry (readers claude-opus-5-5, one per packet, via the CLI; three; seed 20261015; account.md sha256 77b5e35d..., figure, propositions, claims, return spec and the three packets pinned). author_claims.jsonl: nine claims. Rooms by rule (logged before the draw, revised twice for the 50 KB ceiling before any page was read for content): cardinals (told), luciomains (told with a residue), mysterydungeon (late side, which the account visits least: 2 rooms against 7); each served as its facts and 7 passages by cite.py's seeded draw, no forest. RETURN-C5.md: the stage's return line plus declarations and codes for J's ruling 4. The second reading: the rule, the 40 sentences of the 36 amended declarations that the rule's word lists put in question (from the ledger, split by declaration across readers), and the 72 Stigmergy records, 24 per reader, to code blind. Not served: the whole declarations and their other sentences and quotes; QC5-001 asks the handler whether this suffices, and the packets go out meanwhile. Packets 50,998, 51,023 and 51,040 bytes. Slips: order (rooms and RETURN before the manifest entry and claims), a no-op heredoc command, two parallel Edits to one script, the figure naming A21 (fixed, packets rebuilt). validate.py C5: 0 errors, 0 warnings; head 2,994 words, links resolve. Next: done.sh C5 --cut packets-out.

C5c-01 opens (the readers' check, pass 5 of the account). Read AGENT.md, the head, the stage file, diary --last 5, validate.py --open C5 (0 errors, 0 warnings), and QC5-001's answer. J (08:35 Amsterdam): the three fleet packets stand as sent; for the second reading of the declarations, build packages for the field analyst with all 36 amended declarations whole, the rule and the members' quotes each rests on, as many packages as needed, outside the fleet ceiling, written for a reader who was not here. J (09:09) adds that they go to a fork of the field analyst or a fresh session on the same model with the FA field model as context, and that the reader judges each sentence against its members' quotes, not its own model. J (07:59) on my C5a-04 answer: I decide what comes into the model and what goes out of it, by my own criterion. The PI asks me to check whether the dispatch's ~54,000 bytes per packet is the wrapper it adds. This leg: copy the returns into readers-C5/, score fidelity both ways, score the sentence verdicts and the Stigmergy codes against mine, answer every item under rule 13, build the field packages, then close.

The three validated returns copied unchanged into readers-C5/ (C5-reader-1.jsonl to C5-reader-3.jsonl; sha256 of each copy matches its source in _fleet_raw/C5/). Each return names reader r1, since the dispatch ran one reader per packet; the packet name keeps them apart. All three served account.md 77b5e35d..., the digest run_manifest.json records. The dispatch's packet hashes and its return-spec hash match mine: the packets went out as built. The ~54,000 bytes the dispatch printed per packet is the packet with RETURN-C5.md served beside it (50,998 + 2,970 = 53,968 for reader 1); the packet alone is under the 51,200 ceiling.

The readers' Stigmergy codes against mine (c5c_codes_score.py). T3-038 (reader 1): 21 of 24 agree, kappa 0.81; P in 4 of 14 not O against my 5 of 15; the rule is not met either way. T3-041 (reader 2): 15 of 24 agree, kappa 0.48; P in 8 of 14 not O against my 8 of 17, so under the reader's codes T3-041 meets the rule (P at least half of the records not O). T3-060 (reader 3): 20 of 24, kappa 0.75; P in 10 of 20 against my 8 of 20, exactly half, so it meets the rule too. Across the three, trace or marker in 26 of 48 by the readers' codes against my 31 of 52. The decision that kept Stigmergy's cut rests on codes two coders do not agree on, and for two member themes the second coding reverses it. I do not adjudicate my own disagreements with a reader alone: the 72 records go blind to the field analyst as a third coder in the QC5-001 packages, and the cut is decided in a later check pass with three codings in hand. The account says meanwhile that the cut is contested.

account.md pass 5 (C5c-01), answering the readers; pass 4 kept as account-p4.md (sha256 matched). Fixed as author-error: the note on thin and theorised (the thin arrows beat their nulls by 0.009 to 0.041 or rest on 21 rooms; only A11 fails and A12 has no count); the numbers of F-009, F-002 and F-006 put in the text; the counts marked as rooms carrying each theme; the second analyst named by what they did; the template sentence tied to the setting fact; A12 marked theorised in its own paragraph; the Stigmergy read called a sample, with the second coding and the cut said to be open; ultrahardcore's 'no neighbour' now 'no border talk and no upkeep'; ubc's attack call quoted [ubc/c0064]; the residue list said to name rooms told in part, not rooms out of reach; the 34 sentences the readers could not follow rewritten; Stigmergy, story rooms and residue glossed; one conditional answer [cardinals/c0062] named as a range the account does not count. 2,300 words (target line amended). The readers' disagreements printed beside it in account-readers-C5.md (cardinals as the sample showed it; celebration before upkeep; the move with no doubt shown; luciomains on the list), each quote checked against its return.

QC5-001 answered (J, 08:35 and 09:09 Amsterdam): the field analyst's packages for the second reading of the declarations are built in out/field-packages-C5/ (c5c_field_packages.py), outside the fleet ceiling. 00-READ-FIRST.md (who reads: a fork of the field analyst or a fresh session with the field model; judge each sentence against the members' quotes and the rule, not against your own model; what the study is; what to read; what to judge); 01-the-rule.md (the rule whole with its dimension extension and the four setting facts); eight packages by dimension, 02-D01 to 09-D08, with all 36 declarations as they stand, 268 sentences numbered, each declaration's members by name, the quotes it cites or rested on and 3 quotes drawn per member theme by cite.py under seed 20261015; 10-findings.md (the 11 findings the declarations cite, statement and bound); 11-stigmergy-records.md (the 72 Stigmergy records in a seeded order, blind: a third coding); RETURN-field-C5.md; MANIFEST.json (bytes, sha256). 178,359 bytes. Nothing of the fleet readers' returns is served. The ten declarations the fleet packets left out are included. I would rather the field reading come back before I amend the declarations or settle the Stigmergy cut: both wait for it.
